metadata.title: US strikes Iranian tankers after more attempted missile attacks on Navy warship

sources.news_title: US military says it has destroyed 5 Iranian oil tankers after missile attacks on Navy warship

sources.text:
Iran launched a barrage of missiles towards Jordan early Wednesday morning, after US forces struck multiple Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
The missiles were clearly visible across large parts of Israel. Israeli security officials stressed that Israel was not involved in the interception efforts and that no missiles entered Israeli airspace.
Iranian officials confirmed that Iran attacked the Muwaffaq Salti and Prince Hassan military bases in Jordan.
Explosions were also reportedly heard in Bahrain following launches from Iran.
A US official told Reuters on Tuesday evening that the US struck the tankers following attempted missile attacks against a US Navy warship.
According to the official, the strikes were carried out after additional Iranian attempts to launch missiles at the American vessel.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) subsequently announced that its forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers after the IRGC targeted a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days.
“The US warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed," the statement stressed.
The US confirmation followed reports in Iranian media that an Iranian oil tanker was hit near Kharg Island, a key center of Iran's oil exports. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency reported that the vessel was struck by a US missile about four miles from the island.
Tasnim said the tanker was hit while in the anchorage area and that there were no reported casualties. The crew was evacuating the vessel, while Iranian authorities were investigating the incident.
The extent of the damage was not immediately known. Tasnim said additional information would be released as it became available.
A second Iranian vessel was subsequently struck near Kharg Island, according to Iran's state-run Student News Network (SNN), which provided no further details.
Amid the attacks, the IRGC Navy issued a warning to tanker crews operating near ports in Kuwait and Bahrain, ordering them to leave their vessels immediately. The Iranian force said the ships would be targeted in retaliation for the US strikes on Iranian tankers.
“Given the hostile actions of the terrorist US military in targeting several Iranian oil tankers, we warn all tanker crews in the vicinity of ports in Kuwait and Bahrain," the IRGC Navy said in a statement carried by state media.
The statement accused Kuwait and Bahrain of hosting American forces and supporting Washington's actions against Iran. It said the two countries “host these terrorists and are partners in their actions," before warning: “Immediately leave your vessels, whether at anchorage or at the docks, because they will be targeted."
Tuesday’s incident comes a week after American forces carried out attacks around Qeshm Island, Chabahar and Bandar Abbas, near the Strait of Hormuz.
Three days later, on Friday, Trump warned that the US could target Pickaxe Mountain, a heavily fortified Iranian facility where Tehran has allegedly been expanding its nuclear infrastructure.
"Iran will not have a nuclear weapon," Trump said in the Oval Office. He added, "We may hit Pickaxe very soon...if there was anything going on with Pickaxe."
On Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, while Iranian state media reported the following day that Iran had launched a Qassem Basir missile.

Updated on September 8, 2026 at 6:23 pm EST
The US on Tuesday launched more strikes against Iranian oil tankers, and the Iranian military vowed it would respond, marking another escalation of the war.
A US official told Fox News reporter Jennifer Griffin that the US launched strikes against tankers near Kharg Island, deep inside the Persian Gulf, and near the Iranian port city of Jask, on the Gulf of Oman.
US Central Command later claimed that it “destroyed” five Iranian tankers, and said the attacks were a response to Iran targeting a US warship that is enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports.
“The US warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed,” CENTCOM said.
So far, Iranian media has reported that at least one tanker was struck near Kharg Island and that there were no casualties since the crew evacuated. Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi, the chief of the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, said that the US had warned the tankers would be targeted and that Iran would respond.
“The aggressive US army has given Iranian oil tankers a warning to evacuate in order to attack them. So, I declare that any attack on Iranian oil tankers will result in the targeting of US bases in the region by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Abdollahi said, according to Iran’s Mehr news agency.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned that tankers near Kuwait and Bahrain would also be targeted in response and urged crew members to evacuate their vessels, whether they’re in port or at anchor.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said on Sunday, after the US bombed three Iranian tankers on Saturday, that if the US keeps targeting Iran’s oil infrastructure, the Iranian military would target assets belonging to US energy companies in the region.
